questions.stem: The Gupta Empire is often called the 'Golden Age' of India. Who was its founder?
questions.explanation: Sri Gupta (c. 240-280 CE) founded the Gupta dynasty but was a minor king. Ghatotkacha (280-319) followed. But the EMPIRE-builder — the first major imperial Gupta — was CHANDRAGUPTA I (r. 319-335 CE), who took the imperial title 'Maharajadhiraja' and started the GUPTA ERA (319 CE). He married LICCHAVI princess Kumaradevi — a political marriage that greatly enhanced Gupta influence in the Ganga valley. His son SAMUDRAGUPTA (335-375) hugely expanded the empire; called the 'Indian Napoleon' by V. A. Smith. CHANDRAGUPTA II VIKRAMADITYA (375-414) reached Gupta's zenith — defeated Western Kshatrapas, Fa-Hien visited, nine gems 'Navaratna' flourished. Decline after Skandagupta (455-467) who repelled Hun invasions.

questions.stem: Samudragupta's military achievements are inscribed in which famous prashasti (eulogy)?

options.option_text: Allahabad Prashasti (Prayag Prashasti), composed by Harisena

questions.explanation: The ALLAHABAD PRASHASTI (Prayag Prashasti), inscribed on an ASHOKAN PILLAR at Prayag (Allahabad/Prayagraj) by court poet HARISENA, is the primary source on Samudragupta's conquests. In Sanskrit, it lists 4 groups of kings defeated: (1) 9 of Aryavarta (uprooted); (2) 12 of Dakshinapatha (defeated and released — the 'Dharma-vijaya' policy); (3) 5 frontier kingdoms (submission); (4) 9 tribal republics. AIHOLE INSCRIPTION — by Ravikirti for Chalukya Pulakeshin II. MANDSAUR — by Vatsabhatti on Kumaragupta era. JUNAGADH — by Rudradaman (Saka), later appended by Skandagupta recording repair of Sudarshana Lake. Fun fact: the Allahabad pillar originally had Ashoka's edict; Samudragupta, Jahangir, and the British all added inscriptions.

questions.stem: Which Gupta king is associated with the title 'Vikramaditya' and whose court hosted the 'Nine Gems' (Navaratnas)?
questions.explanation: CHANDRAGUPTA II VIKRAMADITYA (r. 375-414 CE) — the Gupta zenith. The 'Nine Gems' (NAVARATNA) at his court (per later tradition) included: KALIDASA (playwright — Abhijnana Shakuntalam, Meghaduta; greatest Sanskrit poet), AMARASIMHA (lexicographer — Amarakosha dictionary), DHANVANTARI (physician), VARAHAMIHIRA (astronomer — Brihat Samhita, Panch Siddhantika), VETALA BHATTA, GHATAKARPARA, SHANKU, KSHAPANAKA, VARARUCHI. FA-HIEN (Chinese Buddhist monk) visited India 405-411 CE, documented Gupta society in 'Fa Guo Ji' (Record of Buddhist Kingdoms). Chandragupta II defeated the Western Kshatrapas (Sakas) and issued silver coins in their style. Also called 'Sakari' (slayer of Sakas). His daughter Prabhavatigupta married the Vakataka king (alliance).

questions.stem: The IRON PILLAR at Delhi (Mehrauli, near Qutb Complex), famous for its rust-resistant composition over 1600+ years, is from which era?
questions.explanation: The Iron Pillar at Mehrauli (Delhi) dates to the Gupta period — inscription on it is in Sanskrit Brahmi script referring to a king 'Chandra' (generally identified as CHANDRAGUPTA II Vikramaditya). ~7 m tall, ~6 tonnes, 98% wrought iron. Its remarkable rust-resistance is due to a thin protective layer of 'misawite' (hydrogen phosphate) formed by catalytic action of phosphorus present in the iron (~1%) reacting with air — a marvel of ancient Indian metallurgy. Originally stood at a Vishnu temple in Udayagiri (MP), later moved to Delhi by Anangpal Tomar or Iltutmish. In the Qutb Complex since 1200s. Iltutmish's Qutb Minar built around it. Another Gupta masterpiece: BHITARI and ERAN pillars, the DASHAVATARA TEMPLE at Deogarh (oldest surviving Hindu stone temple, 500 CE).

questions.stem: ARYABHATA, the astronomer-mathematician who proposed heliocentrism and authored 'Aryabhatiya' in 499 CE, flourished under which dynasty?
questions.explanation: ARYABHATA (476-550 CE) — lived during the later Gupta era under Budhagupta — composed the 'ARYABHATIYA' in 499 CE at age 23 at Kusumapura (Pataliputra). Key contributions: (1) Proposed Earth rotates on its axis (heliocentrism hints); (2) Used place-value notation WITHOUT zero as a written symbol (Brahmagupta, 628 CE, formalised zero and negative numbers); (3) Value of π (pi) ≈ 3.1416, close to modern; (4) Accurate calculation of solar year (365.25858 days); (5) Explained lunar eclipse (moon in Earth's shadow) and solar eclipse rationally (moon blocks sun) against prevailing demonic theories. Other Gupta-era scientists: VARAHAMIHIRA, BRAHMAGUPTA (7th c. actually Post-Gupta but influenced by Gupta tradition), DHANVANTARI. India's first satellite (1975) named 'Aryabhata' in his honour.

questions.stem: The decline of the Gupta Empire began mainly due to invasions by which foreign tribe in the 5th-6th century CE?
questions.explanation: The HUNAS (White Huns / Hephthalites) — a Central Asian nomadic people — invaded India from the NW in the mid-5th c. CE. Initially REPELLED by SKANDAGUPTA (c. 455-467 CE — hailed as 'Vikramaditya' for this victory; Bhitari pillar inscription records it). After Skandagupta's death, subsequent weaker Gupta rulers (Buddhagupta, Narasimhagupta, Vishnugupta) lost ground. Hun chieftains TORAMANA (c. 500 CE, captured Malwa region) and his son MIHIRAKULA (c. 515-540 CE, notorious persecutor of Buddhists — defeated by Yashodharman of Malwa in 528). Gupta fragmentation complete by c. 550 CE. Sakas had been defeated by Chandragupta II earlier (4th c.). Kushans preceded Guptas (1st-3rd c.). Parthians — short-lived 1st c. BCE Indo-Parthian kingdom in NW.

questions.stem: Which of the following is considered the OLDEST surviving Hindu stone temple in India, dating to the Gupta era?
questions.explanation: The DASHAVATARA TEMPLE at Deogarh (Lalitpur district, UP), built c. 500 CE — the oldest surviving Hindu STONE temple in its original form. Dedicated to Vishnu (hence 'Dashavatara' — ten incarnations). Features magnificent relief panels: (1) Gajendra Moksha (rescue of the elephant); (2) Nara-Narayana; (3) Sheshashayi Vishnu (Vishnu on cosmic serpent Ananta). Introduced the SHIKHARA (curvilinear tower) architectural element that became the cornerstone of Nagara temple style. Other early Gupta temples: Tigawa (c. 400 CE) and Sanchi Temple 17 (c. 400 CE) — simpler flat-roof. KAILASA at Ellora (8th c. Rashtrakuta), BRIHADESHWARA (1010 CE Chola), KONARK (13th c. Eastern Ganga) — all much later.
